name: Street Custom 'Lazarus Wire' Garrote System
description: A retractable monofilament garrote concealed within a standard-looking wristwatch or bracelet. The wire extends from a spring-loaded spool hidden in the band, deploying approximately 60cm of cutting filament that can be used as a traditional garrote or whipped as a short-range slashing weapon. The filament is not true monofilament — it is a braided carbon-steel wire approximately 0.3mm in diameter — but it is thin enough to be invisible in low light and sharp enough to cut to bone with moderate pressure. Retraction is automatic when the deployment button is released, rewinding the bloody wire back into the spool.
specifications:
wire length: 60 cm deployed
wire diameter: 0.3mm braided carbon-steel
cutting depth: Through soft tissue to bone with 5 kg pressure
deployment: Spring-loaded spool, 0.4 second extension
retraction: Automatic on release
concealment: Standard wristwatch or bracelet housing
weight: 0.08 kg total assembly
story_hooks: A series of strangulation murders across multiple tiers share identical wound signatures — the wire diameter and cutting pattern match a single manufacturer's output.
A fashion brand has unknowingly begun selling bracelets that contain Lazarus Wire mechanisms — the items were inserted into their supply chain by an unknown party.

physical_description.visual_profile: An innocuous analog wristwatch or minimalist bracelet that betrays no hint of its lethal purpose. The face is clean and functional, the band appears standard, but the internal spring-loaded spool and deployment mechanism add barely perceptible weight and thickness to the case.
physical_description.dimensions: Watch case: 38mm diameter, 12mm thick. Band width: 18mm. Deployed wire length: 60cm. Wire diameter: 0.3mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light on the wrist—barely noticeable until you move it and feel the subtle resistance of the tensioned spool. Balanced despite the coiled filament; not front-heavy or awkward.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium or surgical steel case, with a polymer or silicone band. The internal spool is aircraft-grade aluminum with reinforced steel bearings.
physical_description.finish: Matte brushed steel case with a minimal dial. The band shows subtle wear from daily use. No visible seams betray the deployment mechanism—engineering is seamless and professional.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray case with a black dial face. Band in black or dark gray polymer. The hidden filament catches ambient light as a faint silver glint only when extended.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth, slightly curved case fits snugly against the wrist. Band is soft silicone or rubberized for comfort and to muffle sound during deployment. No sharp edges; ergonomics prioritize concealment over tactical feel.
distinctive_features: Virtually indistinguishable from a legitimate chronograph watch
Miniature deployment button disguised as the crown or integrated into the band clasp—requires specific pressure sequence to activate
Hairline seams around the case back where the spool mechanism is housed
Faint mechanical click when the spring-loaded spool tensions during deployment
Retracted wire creates a barely visible bulge in the case—noticeable only to trained eye
When deployed, the carbon-steel filament catches light with an opalescent sheen; stained wire shows dark residue that doesn't wash clean easily
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom logo subtly etched into the case back—small enough to pass casual inspection. Serial number laser-etched on the internal spool, invisible without opening the case. No warranties or documentation visible; the weapon is built for plausible deniability.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-used examples show patina on the case from skin oils and handling. The band may be worn smooth. Extended filament often retains faint blood staining in the braided weave—evidence of previous deployment. Most street users never fully clean the spool, treating the residue as a warning to others.

image_prompt: Close-up product photography of a matte gunmetal wristwatch on dark charcoal surface, styled as a neo-noir weapon catalog entry. The watch face is clean and minimal, lying slightly tilted. A single gloved hand—chrome-plated tactical glove—holds the band gently, fingers near the concealed deployment button. The hidden deployment mechanism is subtly emphasized through dramatic side-lighting that catches the edge of the case, creating a sharp shadow that hints at the spool housing beneath. In the background, a thin retracted wisp of carbon-steel filament is visible in sharp focus, slightly bloody and catching reflected light with an opalescent sheen. The overall aesthetic is clinical and dangerous—luxury precision engineering weaponized. Overhead rim lighting emphasizes the titanium finish. --ar 3:2 --v 6
